Series XXIII: Pride and Progress / The Right Stuff

Pride and Progress News-highlights: 1. Gay Week in Review, with Andy Humm, Darrell Yates Rist, Kitty Cotter, and Jim Levin 2. Short news stories 3. Gay Catholic group petitions New York City for the right to demonstrate outside of St. Patrick's Cathedral 4. Discussion of publicly-closeted gay politicians courting the gay vote 5. Accurate government reporting of AIDS, and the privacy issues involved in listing AIDS on death certificates COMMERCIAL: Stamp Out AIDS featuring Jennifer Bassey 6. Andy Humm on Reagan's Education secretary, William Bennett, opposing AIDS Education programs in schools 7. News Watch, Colorado lawmakers ready to approve the testing, tracing, and quarantining individuals suspected of being infected with HIV 8. San Francisco, Chronicle discloses its policy prohibiting the listing of surviving lovers in death notices 9. ACLU considering suing nursing homes in Illinois that refuse to accept persons with AIDS 10. Dutch National Broadcasting Service has begun a television service for lesbians and gay men 11. Paper finds that certain DNA viruses have the ability to activate latent AIDS viruses 12. Senator Edward Kennedy promises adequate AIDS budget beyond Reagan's lackluster budget 13. Sports Report 14. New segment Lavender Health, presented by the Office of Gay and Lesbian Health Concerns of the New York City Department of Health, discussion of AIDS-phobia COMMERCIAL: "First Hand" gay magazine 15. George Trahanis interviews Jeff Goodman, Secretary of the Board of the Greater Gotham Business Council 16. Closing credits
The Right Stuff: 1. This Week in Gay History, with Jeff Bixby COMMERCIAL: "Manscape" gay magazine COMMERCIAL: The Monster 2. GCN Cincinnati TV episode, "Georgia Vice" COMMERCIAL: Zamir Furs 3. Show Bits with George Trahanis, review of Broadway musical "Beehive" 4. COMMERCIAL: Night of a Thousand Gowns charity ball 5. Olivia Negron interviews Gerard Ilaria, a volunteer social worker at New York Hospital and Columbia University Gay Health Advocacy Project 6. Razor Sharp introduces a contest to win a date with her
